author_or_org: Markus Borg, Dave Hewett, Donald Graham, Noric Couderc, Emma Söderberg, Luke Church, Dave Farley

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The source says prior work has highlighted productivity improvements from AI assistants like GitHub Copilot, but this registered report does not itself report controlled-study productivity results.
claims.quote: [Background/Context] AI assistants like GitHub Copilot are transforming software engineering; several studies have highlighted productivity improvements.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The source states that the impact of AI assistants on code quality, particularly maintainability, requires further investigation.
claims.quote: However, their impact on code quality, particularly in terms of maintainability, requires further investigation.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The proposed study aims to examine how AI assistants affect software maintainability and developers' ability to evolve code.
claims.quote: [Objective/Aim] This study aims to examine the influence of AI assistants on software maintainability, specifically assessing how these tools affect the ability of developers to evolve code.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The planned two-phased controlled experiment involves professional developers; Phase 1 adds a Java feature with or without an AI assistant, and Phase 2 is a randomized controlled trial in which different developers evolve random Phase 1 projects without AI assistants.
claims.quote: [Method] We will conduct a two-phased controlled experiment involving professional developers. In Phase 1, developers will add a new feature to a Java project, with or without the aid of an AI assistant. Phase 2, a randomized controlled trial, will involve a different set of developers evolving random Phase 1 projects - working without AI assistants.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The study plans to use Bayesian analysis to evaluate differences in completion time, perceived productivity, code quality, and test coverage.
claims.quote: We will employ Bayesian analysis to evaluate differences in completion time, perceived productivity, code quality, and test coverage.
